title: Customer escalation: fastpath telemetry and safe bailout for hosted API timeout waves
creator: Ava Chen
description: High-severity customer escalations (multiple tenants) during sustained request surges exposed a dangerous interplay: long tail timeouts at the hosted edge + backend KV cache thrash + aggressive client retries. Impact: repeated 5xx/timeouts, customer-visible failed requests, and escalation tickets from three enterprise customers. This ticket scopes a pragmatic mitigation (safe-bailout fastpath) that: 1) gives customers a deterministic, SDK-friendly response when we're overloaded instead of opaque 5xx; 2) introduces lightweight telemetry anchors to speed triage; 3) implements a short-term tenant-scoped admission shim and fallback to lighter model variants while we root-cause and fix KV/cache scheduling issues.
context: Observed pattern: a small cohort of tenants with large batch fanout triggered KV cache compaction and kernel scheduling contention on a subset of inference hosts. Client SDKs retried aggressively (no idempotency tokens), amplifying in-flight load and causing cascading timeouts. Current symptoms: 5xx spikes, streaming stalls, long tail latencies >10s, and increased error rates flagged by SLA monitors. Customers reported partial responses and opaque errors that prevented graceful recovery in their apps.
goal: Mitigate customer impact immediately while we investigate root causes. Provide deterministic, machine-readable fallback responses and telemetry so support + eng can correlate incidents quickly. Reduce visible 5xx/timeouts by 70% for affected tenants within rollout window and provide a follow-up engineering plan to eliminate underlying KV/host contention.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout of safe-bailout fastpath in us-west1 with 95% of canary traffic returning fallback behavior for overloaded requests
Dashboard tile showing fallback activation rate, average tail latency, and tenant attribution; alerts thresholded for >1% fallback rate per tenant/hour
SDK guidance and sample error payload documented; client teams can detect fallback and implement local degraded UX
Post-rollout telemetry shows >=70% reduction in customer-visible 5xx/timeouts for targeted tenants
Postmortem action items created for KV cache scheduling, request shaping, and long-term mitigation tracked in Hosted Stability Initiative
steps_taken: 2026-03-01: Incident triage with Support and Customer Success for Acme and TwinApps — captured request traces and tenant heatmap
2026-03-01: Short-term mitigation idea: edge-level fastfail that returns structured fallback with guidance for clients (safe_bailout) instead of opaque 5xx

2026-03-02: Implemented edge admission shim (edge-circuit-admission) to fastfail requests exceeding 3000ms backend wait; returns 200 with structured JSON payload and error_code 'SAFE_BAILOUT' for SDKs that opt-in
2026-03-02: Added lightweight telemetry anchors to request path: request_fingerprint, shard_trace_id, tenant_tag to make correlation 1-click in dashboards
2026-03-03: Canary deploy to us-west1 at 5% traffic for high-risk tenants + manual smoke tests against streaming and non-streaming endpoints
2026-03-03: Added fallback route to lightweight model variant (quantized, smaller context) for degraded requests to preserve useful partial responses
2026-03-04: Gradual ramp to 25% in us-west1 + integration test run that validates idempotency-token passthrough and no double-charging behavior
2026-03-05: Created runbook and customer comm templates for Support to explain fallback behavior and SDK guidance
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary us-west1 (5% per-tenant) -> Phase 1: Ramp to 25% and monitor fallback/latency -> Phase 2: Region expand (us-east1, europe-west1) with 10% ramp per region -> Phase 3: Full rollout for affected tenant classes, then enable auto-detection for future surges. Rollback gate: if error-rate or dropped tokens increase by >10% vs baseline or any data integrity concern, immediate rollback to previous routing.
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: 'SafeBailout / Fastpath' with panels for fallback activation by tenant, tail latency percentiles, backend wait histogram, idempotency token distribution, and correlation links to trace viewer. Alerts: fallback_rate_per_tenant > 1% in 15m, tail_latency_99p > 2s after fallback activation.
testing_plan: Automated integration tests for streaming/non-streaming endpoints verifying fallback payloads; chaos tests that simulate KV compaction and node-level CPU contention to validate fallback triggers; load test to validate that fastpath reduces tail load and prevents retry amplification.
mitigation_duration_estimate: 2 weeks for short-term fastpath rollout and canary validation; 6-8 weeks for root cause fixes and KV scheduler improvements
next_steps: 1) Complete canary validation (by 2026-03-08). 2) Engage Runtime team for KV scheduling deep-dive and sequence-length kernel selection audit. 3) Coordinate SDK owners for opt-in safe_bailout handling and idempotency token recommendations. 4) Schedule postmortem and update SLO docs.
